blocks.text: [F] Indo-MIM makes small, complex precision metal components, mainly by metal injection moulding (MIM), with additional capability in investment casting, precision machining, ceramic injection moulding, 3D printing, powder manufacturing, electronics assembly and trading (AR2026 p.22, p.61). [F] It earns revenue mainly from selling parts (Rs 3,942.8 cr of FY26 operating revenue of Rs 4,193.0 cr), plus tooling income (Rs 120.9 cr), engineering services (Rs 77.3 cr), export incentives (Rs 36.3 cr) and scrap (Rs 15.6 cr) (AR2026 p.254). [MC] Management describes itself as housing the world's largest installed MIM capacity across more than one million sq ft, serving 650+ customers in 45+ countries and shipping 300M+ parts a year (AR2026 p.4, p.8).

items: [F] End markets named: automotive, defence, medical, aerospace and consumer products, plus metal powders, tooling and traded products (AR2026 p.61). [F] The table of revenue by end-use industry that the MD&A introduces is blank in the filed annual report, so **no end-market % split is disclosed** in the documents available (AR2026 p.62).

[F] Geography: FY26 product revenue was Rs 904.1 cr domestic (21.8%) and Rs 3,237.0 cr exports (78.2%), against Rs 284.5 cr (8.7%) and Rs 2,993.9 cr (91.3%) in FY25 (AR2026 p.254, p.272). [E] Domestic sales roughly tripled (+218%) in one year, and the documents give no explanation.

[F] Manufacturing is concentrated in India: MIM at Hoskote and Doddaballapur (Bangalore), investment casting at Tirupati, and a new Chennai plant that had 'just now commenced' operations. Overseas units are in San Antonio (MIM), Arizona (Triax casting and machining), the UK (Conway Marsh Garrett MIM) and California (Phoenix DeVentures medical prototyping), plus a 49%-owned secondary-operations entity in Mexico (AR2026 p.7, p.39). [F] The group reports 15 manufacturing facilities (AR2026 p.68).

[F] Customer profile: no customer is named and no concentration figure (top 1/5/10) is disclosed. [MC] Management says it is 'the sole supplier to our customers in most cases' (AR2026 p.40) and judges receivable concentration risk 'low' (AR2026 p.283).

blocks.text: [F] Listing status: Indo-MIM listed on NSE and BSE on 30 July 2026 (AR2026 p.75, p.77). [F] Only one quarter of shareholding data (July 2026) and three quarterly P&L columns are in our statements data (NUMBERS). [F] The prospectus (DRHP/RHP) and any earnings-call transcript were **not available** for this report, so IPO size, use of proceeds, offer-for-sale amounts, lock-ins and any IPO-era guidance cannot be verified. [AI] The evidence base is the FY26 annual report (prepared largely while the company was unlisted), one listed quarter of numbers and exchange announcements.

items: 1. **Valuation leaves no room for error.** [F] At Rs 1,242 the stock trades at 115.1x trailing earnings and 58.6x EV/EBITDA; our DCF gives Rs 58.9 / Rs 109.8 / Rs 155.7 per share in bear / base / bull, and the reverse DCF implies 98.8% annual sales growth for five years (NUMBERS).

2. **Profit growth has lagged revenue for five years.** [F] Sales 5-year CAGR is 16.2%, EBITDA 4.6% and PAT -0.7%; OPM fell from 43% (FY21) to 26% (FY26) (NUMBERS). [F] The documents do not explain the compression.

3. **Acquisitions have destroyed value.** [F] Conway Marsh Garrett goodwill is fully impaired (Rs 12.0 cr in FY25, Rs 71.1 cr in FY26) about three years after a Rs 105.6 cr purchase; Triax PPE was impaired by Rs 103.1 cr in FY25; Phoenix DeVentures added Rs 112.8 cr of goodwill against Rs 12.6 cr of net assets and lost USD 2.9 mn pre-tax in FY26 (AR2026 p.23, p.234-235, p.259, p.274).

4. **Promoter-family pay is very large.** [F] FY26 remuneration was Rs 56.8 cr for the Chairman & MD and Rs 38.2 cr for the CEO (AR2026 p.277). [E] Together that is about 17.8% of consolidated PAT of Rs 533.5 cr.

5. **Control weaknesses around inventory.** [F] Inventory reported to banks differed from books by Rs 56-92 cr every quarter of FY26, receivables by up to Rs 42 cr (attributed to a 'clerical error' in December 2025). The inventory software has no audit trail, and the accounting software logs no database-level changes (AR2026 p.118, p.284, p.218).

6. **Quality of FY26 cash flow and earnings is mixed.** [F] FY26 other income included Rs 80.2 cr of FX gain and Rs 36.9 cr of compensation from customers for cancelled contracts (AR2026 p.256); CFO benefited from a Rs 110.7 cr fall in other current assets, mainly statutory balances (AR2026 p.227, p.244).

7. **Large ESOP pool and thin free float.** [F] Shareholders ratified an ESOP pool of up to 7.23 cr options at an exercise price that can be as low as Re 1 (AR2026 p.80, p.101; ANNOUNCEMENTS). [E] That equals about 14.6% of the 49.47 cr shares outstanding (NUMBERS). [F] Promoters hold 77.65%, FIIs 2.34% (NUMBERS).

8. **Tax disputes are rising.** [F] Contingent liabilities rose to Rs 227.4 cr from Rs 127.8 cr, including a Rs 67.6 cr income-tax dispute over the concessional 22% rate and GST demands of Rs 64.8 cr (RCM) and Rs 27.4 cr (AR2026 p.122, p.270).
9. **Disclosure is thin for a Rs 61,000 cr company.** [F] No segment reporting, no end-market split, no customer concentration, no capacity or utilisation, no order book (AR2026 p.61-62, p.272).
10. **US tariff and localisation risk.** [MC] Management calls US tariffs on Indian products 'a new emerging threat' (AR2026 p.42), and the business is about 78% exports (AR2026 p.254).

blocks.text: [AI] The industrial case is credible: a 30-year founder-built MIM business with Rs 4,193 cr revenue, 25% ROCE and an AA+ rating (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.69). The market price is a different matter. It requires growth no historical period supports: 98.8% implied CAGR against 16.2% achieved over five years (NUMBERS). Two disclosures the market may be overlooking cut against the narrative. First, the ESOP fair value used for the December 2024 grant was Rs 35 per share (AR2026 p.268). Second, five-year PAT growth is negative (NUMBERS). The opposite risk also exists: if the Q1 FY27 margin of 33% and the domestic surge prove durable, earnings could compound faster than the trailing record suggests. Even the bull DCF (Rs 155.7) is far below the price, so the variant view is not 'cheap or expensive by a little'. It is that the price is not anchored in disclosed fundamentals.

[AI] The core MIM business is 30 years old, which makes this a mature franchise, not a start-up. The 'growth adjacencies' are recent: Triax (2020), Conway (2023), Phoenix (2025), the Arms subsidiary (Dec 2025) and the Chennai plant (just commenced). [F] The annual report gives no customer concentration data. The auditor's segment note does not identify any single customer at 10% or more of revenue, and management calls receivable concentration risk 'low' (AR2026 p.272, p.283). [AI] Read both ways: (a) 650+ customers suggests a long tail; (b) 'sole supplier in most cases' (AR2026 p.40), a domestic stream that tripled with no explanation, and Rs 36.9 cr of contract-cancellation compensation from customers (AR2026 p.256) suggest individual programmes can be large. Concentration may be meaningful, but it cannot be measured.
